title: Comparing decimals

cues.caption: Amy's bean plant grew 0.4 metres. Ben's grew 0.35 metres. Whose plant grew more?

cues.caption: What do you think? Have a go in your head.

cues.caption: Ben says his grew more, because 35 is bigger than 4. But is a longer number always bigger?
cues.say: Ben says his grew more, because thirty five is bigger than four. [pause] But is a longer number always bigger?

cues.caption: Let's use place-value columns. 0.4 has 4 tenths. 0.35 has 3 tenths and 5 hundredths.
cues.say: Let's use place-value columns. Nought point four has four tenths. [pause] Nought point three five has three tenths, and five hundredths.

cues.caption: Compare the biggest place first: the tenths. 4 tenths is more than 3 tenths. So 0.4 is bigger!
cues.say: Compare the biggest place first. That's the tenths. [pause] Four tenths is more than three tenths. So nought point four is bigger!

cues.caption: Here's a trick: fill the gap with a zero. 0.4 is the same as 0.40: forty hundredths. 0.35 is thirty-five hundredths.

cues.say: On a hundred square, nought point four fills forty squares. And nought point three five fills thirty five. [pause] Amy's plant grew more!

cues.caption: The rule: line up the points, fill gaps with zeros, then compare from the left.
cues.say: So here's the rule. Line up the points. Fill gaps with zeros. [pause] Then compare from the left.
